title: BYD Says Actively Reviewing Korea Launch of Shark Pickup Truck
snippet: BYD signaled new model launches in Korea, including the Shark pickup truck, at the 2026 Busan Mobility Show, while debuting its 37.5 million won Sealion 6
extractedText: BYD Says Actively Reviewing Korea Launch of Shark Pickup TruckPress Briefing at Busan Mobility Show Lineup Expansion Signaled After PHEV Liu Xueliang: "Cooperating with Korean Firms Centered on Vehicle Software Including TMap Navigation, FLO, KakaoMap"Finance|Published 2026.06.28. 17:36:33|By Kim Woo-bo|Summary|SaveAAALiu Xueliang, General Manager of BYD's Asia-Pacific Auto Sales Division. BYD KoreaBYD, which has stepped up its push into the Korean market by unveiling a plug-in hybrid vehicle (PHEV) priced in the 37 million won range, has signaled the additional launch of new models such as a pickup truck.BYD held a press briefing at the "2026 Busan Mobility Show," which opened Friday at BEXCO in Busan's Haeundae district, and announced plans including new vehicle launches.Ding Hai Mihao, head of BYD Korea, said in response to a question about whether the "Shark" pickup truck would be launched domestically, "If consumers want it, we will actively review it." Regarding plans to introduce BYD's premium brand "Yangwang," Liu Xueliang, general manager of BYD's Asia-Pacific automotive sales division, said, "We are not reviewing it at the moment," but added, "If the opportunity arises, we have plans to bring it in."BYD, which first entered the Korean market last year, has been increasing sales centered on mid- to low-priced electric vehicles such as the "Atto 3" and "Sealion," and over the long term it aims to expand its domestic market share by adding pickup trucks and premium cars to its lineup.At this year's Busan Mobility Show, BYD diversified its powertrain lineup by unveiling the plug-in hybrid vehicle (PHEV) "Sealion 6 DM-i" in Korea for the first time. The new vehicle was priced at 37.5 million won, similar to or lower than domestic mid-size hybrid sport utility vehicles (SUVs), signaling aggressive sales. General Manager Liu said, "We priced it so that more consumers can experience (BYD vehicles)."BYD said it is strengthening cooperation with Korean companies centered on vehicle software. General Manager Liu explained, "TMap navigation and the music platform FLO can be used in BYD vehicles," adding, "The Sealion 6 DM-i is equipped with KakaoMap."The company will also continue to expand its domestic showrooms and service centers. General Manager Liu said, "It has only been one year since we entered Korea, so consumers do not know BYD well," adding, "We will hold test-drive events nationwide and various events such as a 'fuel-efficiency challenge' to promote BYD's technology."Liu Xueliang, General Manager of BYD's Asia-Pacific Auto Sales Division.
